analysis:
The PR is documentation-only: one table row is added to docs/provider/cli-reference.md (head line 1751) for the LaunchAgent environment passthrough list. It documents DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP, read in ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift (`shapeWarmupEnvironmentKey`). `0` disables the load-time shape warmup and `always` skips its shader-cache probe. No executable code, protocol message, key handling, attestation path or authorization logic changes in the supplied evidence.

Threat-model relevance: the row sits in the table of variables that `darkbloom start` copies from the invoking shell into the provider plist (cited from LaunchAgent.swift `passthroughEnvKeys`/`inferencePassthroughEnvKeys`). The documented knob only affects performance and TTFT calibration. It is operator-controlled, and the operator is already ADV-001 inside TB-003. It does not touch the prefix cache policy, the SSD cache TTL, HMAC lookup names, KEK handling or cacheSalt scoping (T-041 / SEC-035), nor App Attest or serving authorization (TB-011, T-053/T-054).

Unverified contracts for integration: (1) the Swift source that actually reads this variable and whether LaunchAgent.swift forwards it into the plist are not supplied, so the doc row is not confirmed against code. (2) Warmup timing could in principle alter TTFT characteristics relevant to the accepted SEC-035 timing oracle. That depends on the implementation and is not evidenced here, so it is not reported as a finding. No threat-model update is required from this doc change alone.
